4 Common Problems Nurses Face and How To Handle Them

A career in nursing offers profound rewards through the opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of others every day. Nurses, like yourself have the privilege of providing compassionate care, comfort, and support to patients during their most vulnerable moments.

You don’t only get fulfillment from taking care of other people. You also get monetary benefits like competitive salaries, generous benefits packages, and opportunities for overtime and shift differences. 

As rewarding as the profession can be, it doesn’t come without its unique set of challenges.

Daunting careers like nursing are characterized by high responsibility, demanding both emotional and physical commitment.

Nurses, like yourself navigate complex medical conditions, heavy workloads, and strict regulatory requirements every day.

You should learn to overcome these challenges to maintain focus on patient care, foster personal well-being, and enhance job satisfaction.

By developing resilience and problem-solving skills, you can prevent burnout, ensure patient safety, and earn professional respect.

If you are interested in contributing to a positive work environment, then you should read further.

In this blog post, we will be having a look at some of the common problems nurses face and provide practical tips on how to handle them effectively.

Common Problems Nurses Face and How To Handle Them

Here are some challenges nurses face and how to handle them.

1. Heavy Workloads:

A heavy workload can mean caring for a large number of patients with diverse needs. Balancing administrative tasks alongside patient care. Facing time constraints due to scheduling or staffing issues. Managing emotionally challenging situations, and handling complex medical cases.

These situations can contribute to stress, fatigue, and difficulty maintaining quality care and personal well-being. 

Solution to Heavy Workloads

To manage heavy workloads effectively as a nurse, you can start by prioritizing tasks based on urgency and patient needs.

By prioritizing tasks, you can ensure critical interventions are addressed promptly while still managing or handing off less urgent responsibilities. 

You should also consider utilizing time management techniques, like setting realistic goals. Utilizing prioritization tools, and minimizing distractions, so you can work better and be more productive amidst demanding schedules. 

Also, collaborations are a great way to get things done in no time. Consider collaborating with your colleagues to share responsibilities and support one another.

This will help you manage workload fluctuations and become a better team player within your healthcare team.

2. Emotional Stress:

Emotional stress caused by the demanding nature of the nursing profession is a significant challenge.

These demands can range from long hours to high patient volumes, and even complex cases.

Dealing with these demands while being in emotionally charged situations, such as patient suffering, trauma, and loss, can take a toll on your mental and emotional well-being.

You may begin to feel sad, helpless, or even grief after witnessing patients in pain or experiencing adverse outcomes. 

The feeling of being overwhelmed by the intensity of your work environment and struggling to find time for self-care and revitalization is a very common problem faced by nurses.

Additionally, the pressure to provide compassionate care while managing your own emotions can lead to emotional exhaustion and burnout.

Solution to Emotional Stress

When dealing with emotional stress, an important strategy to employ is setting boundaries as much as possible.

Some boundaries you can establish in the work environment may include establishing limits on work hours. Balancing workload to avoid feeling overwhelmed.

Also, managing emotional involvement with patients by practicing self-care and seeking support when needed. And communicating their needs effectively to supervisors and colleagues. 

You can also employ various coping strategies, such as seeking support from colleagues, supervisors, or counseling services, and engaging in stress-reduction activities like mindfulness or exercise.

By acknowledging and addressing what situations, events, or circumstances can evoke negative emotions or strain your mental and emotional well-being, it will be easier for you to manage your mental and emotional health. 

3. Busy Schedule and Work-Life Balance:

As a nurse, your life is characterized by demanding schedules and a constant juggling act between work and personal commitments. 

Let’s talk a walk through your schedule. You’re rotating shifts with long hours, and weekend or holiday work.

The unscripted changes these arrangements can cause can disrupt your sleep patterns.

In addition, it can make it challenging to maintain a consistent routine, leaving little room for predictability in your schedule.

You are required to stay alert and focused throughout your 8-12-hour shifts while managing a wide range of patient needs and medical emergencies.

You may even get to work overtime or be on-call for additional shifts, further adding to your workload and fatigue. 

It gets more and more difficult to maintain a healthy work-life balance due to demanding schedules and long hours.  

Solution to Busy Schedule and Work-Life Balance

Maintaining a healthy balance between work and your personal life while tending to your busy schedule will need a level of commitment from your end.

You will need to prioritize self-care and be accountable for the healthy decisions you will make. 

You should also demand for fair scheduling, set boundaries between work and personal life.

And make time for activities outside of work that bring joy and relaxation. Like hanging out with your friends, going on a solo date, journaling, or taking a stroll.

Read here >>> How To Prepare For a 12-Hour Shift

4. Occupational Fatigue:

The physical demands of nursing, such as long hours on your feet and frequent lifting and transferring of patients.

This goes especially for entry-level nurses, and can cause, musculoskeletal injuries, and overall discomfort. And these can in turn take a toll on your overall health. 

Additionally, chronic fatigue and exhaustion resulting from long shifts and heavy workloads can impact your energy levels, mental health, and ability to perform effectively.

Without proper attention and support to address these physical challenges, you may become unsatisfied with your job. Also, continuously come up with excuses to be late or absent. And ultimately compromise both your personal health and the quality of your patient’s care.

Solution to Occupational Fatigue:

To handle the physical demands caused by your profession, prioritize self-care practices like regular stretching and exercise to improve your strength and flexibility.

You should also invest in supportive footwear and ergonomic equipment to reduce strain on your body. 

Don’t hesitate to ask for assistance when needed and practice proper body mechanics to prevent injuries.

Here’s the thing!

You don’t have to get by any of these challenges nurses often face alone!
